title: Bhooth Bangla Just Had the Biggest Fifth Week in Bollywood History. It Earned More in Week 5 Than Every Other Hindi Film's Week 5 Combined. NRIs Who Skipped It in Theatres Have One More Weekend.
excerpt: The horror-comedy has grossed ₹256 crore worldwide and ₹171 crore in India after 35 days, with no signs of slowing. Its fifth-week collection of ₹7.15 crore is more than double Sooryavanshi's previous record. It's now the third biggest Bollywood film of 2026.
body:
Most Bollywood films are done after three weeks. The big ones — the Dhurandhars, the Borders — hold on for four. Making serious money in a fifth week requires something that budgets can't buy and marketing can't manufacture: an audience that keeps telling other people to go.

Bhooth Bangla just completed its fifth week with ₹7.15 crore in India. To understand how absurd that number is, here are the previous Week 5 records for Bollywood:

  1. Bhooth Bangla — ₹7.15 crore
  2. Sooryavanshi — ₹2.98 crore
  3. Jolly LLB 3 — ₹2.00 crore
  4. OMG 2 — ₹0.97 crore
  5. Sky Force — ₹0.70 crore

It's not just the best Week 5. It's more than double the previous record holder. It's more than the next four films combined.

Where It Stands

After 35 days in theatres, Bhooth Bangla's India net collection stands at ₹171.45 crore. The India gross has crossed ₹203 crore. Overseas, the film has earned ₹53.66 crore. The worldwide total: ₹256.87 crore.

That makes it the third highest-grossing Bollywood film of 2026, behind only Dhurandhar 2 (₹1,184 crore net in India — a different stratosphere entirely) and Border 2 (₹362 crore). It's comfortably ahead of O'Romeo (₹83 crore), Mardaani 3 (₹52 crore), and everything else.

On BookMyShow alone, it has sold 3.20 million tickets — placing it seventh all-time for the 2025-26 season.

The Numbers That Tell the Story

In its fifth week, Bhooth Bangla ran across 16,635 shows nationwide — that's 2,376 shows per day, 35 days after release. Average occupancy for the week was 14.28%, which sounds low until you realize that Week 5 occupancy for most films is literally zero because they've been pulled from theatres.

The weekend-weekday pattern is textbook for a film running on word-of-mouth. Sunday peaked at 21% occupancy with ₹1.90 crore. Monday dropped to ₹0.70 crore. Tuesday, interestingly, bounced back to ₹0.90 crore — a sign that audience discovery is still happening, not fading.

In the national multiplex chains (PVR, INOX, Cinepolis), the film sold 30,180 tickets in Week 5 — nearly half its Week 4 figure of 56,592. In a typical release, Week 5 is less than a tenth of Week 4. Bhooth Bangla is holding at 53%.

Why the Horror-Comedy Formula Works

This isn't a fluke. It's a pattern.

Stree (2018) proved that horror-comedy could be a genuine commercial force in Bollywood. Stree 2 (2025) turned it into a franchise category with ₹527+ crore. Bhool Bhulaiyaa 2 and 3 kept the momentum going. Now Bhooth Bangla has joined the club — and it's doing it with the kind of legs that even the franchise films didn't have.

The genre works because it solves Bollywood's oldest problem: how do you get families into theatres? Romances alienate the dads. Action films lose the moms. Dramas lose the kids. A horror-comedy that delivers genuine scares and genuine laughs hits every quadrant simultaneously. Add the Indian cultural fascination with ghosts, haunted houses, and the supernatural, and you have a genre that's essentially recession-proof.

What NRIs Should Know

If you're in the diaspora and you skipped Bhooth Bangla — it's still in theatres. At 2,300+ daily shows after 35 days, you likely still have a screen near you. The overseas gross of ₹53+ crore confirms that NRI audiences have been turning up, but the film's domestic performance suggests there's still discovery happening.

The OTT window for Bhooth Bangla hasn't been officially announced, but based on the industry-standard eight-week theatrical exclusivity period, expect it to land on a streaming platform by late June or early July. Given the film's performance, it'll likely be one of the highest-profile OTT premieres of the summer.

The Bottom Line

Bhooth Bangla isn't the biggest Bollywood film of 2026. It's not going to challenge Dhurandhar 2's absurd numbers. But it might be the healthiest — a film that found its audience organically, held screens through five competitive weeks, and proved once again that you don't need a ₹300 crore budget or a pre-existing franchise to make serious money in Indian cinema.

You just need a good haunted house and a sense of humour.
nri_angle: For NRIs who missed Bhooth Bangla in theatres, the film is still playing — 35 days in, it's still averaging 2,300+ shows per day across India. The horror-comedy genre that began with Stree has become the most reliable money-maker in Bollywood, and Bhooth Bangla is the latest proof. Overseas collections have crossed ₹53 crore.
author: Diaspora Desk
